documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care medicine
documents.body:
Regional medical center
Admitted 04/12/2026, discharged 04/18/2026
Patient: Bernard Bennett, 70 M
Service: medical ICU, then medicine floor

Principal diagnosis: Hypertensive emergency.
Secondary: Cyanide toxicity from sodium nitroprusside. Acute rise in creatinine on chronic kidney disease with the hypertensive emergency.
Chronic: hypertension, chronic kidney disease, mild neurocognitive disorder, primary myelofibrosis on ruxolitinib, carotid sinus hypersensitivity, chronic bronchitis, BPH, urethral stricture, Paget disease of left tibia, lumbar spondylosis.
Allergies: NKDA.

Course:
He came to the ED on the evening of 4/12 with a severe headache and a blood pressure of 226/128. Creatinine 2.5, BUN 40. With renal involvement this was treated as a hypertensive emergency and he went to the ICU on a sodium nitroprusside infusion.

After about 48 hours on nitroprusside (4/14), nursing reported that he had become steadily more agitated and confused. He described a severe headache and looked flushed, and his wife thought he was breathing harder than normal. BP 145/90, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air. Arterial gas pH 7.35, PaCO2 45, PaO2 85. Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 2.8 (2.5 on admission), BUN 55, lactate 5 mmol/L. ECG: sinus tachycardia without other abnormality. Venous cyanide sent.

Cyanide toxicity was diagnosed clinically. Nitroprusside was stopped, hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV was given, and blood pressure control was switched to a nicardipine infusion. Lactate 1.6 the next morning. Confusion and headache cleared within a day and his wife felt he was back to himself. The cyanide level returned 4/16 at 1.1 mg/L, confirming the diagnosis.

He transitioned to oral therapy; amlodipine 5 mg daily added to his home regimen. Creatinine improved to 1.6 by discharge. BP at discharge 142/86.

Discharge medications:
- amlodipine 5 mg daily (NEW)
- lisinopril 10 mg daily
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily
- tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily
- ruxolitinib 5 mg twice daily
- vitamin D3 1,000 units daily
- acetaminophen 500 mg as needed

Follow-up: primary care within one week with a BMP. Hematology as scheduled.

Critical care / hospital medicine

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transitional care call, 2 business days after discharge. Spoke with pt and wife. Home since Saturday. Headache gone, thinking clear, wife agrees. Picked up amlodipine; reviewed full med list against the discharge summary, matches. Home BP this morning 136/82. Visit booked Friday 4/24 with BMP. ED for severe headache, confusion, chest pain or BP over 180.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Discharge summary reviewed in full.
Admitted 4/12-4/18: hypertensive emergency (226/128, creatinine 2.5), treated with nitroprusside in the ICU; at 48 h developed agitation, confusion, headache, flushing and a lactate of 5; cyanide toxicity, confirmed by a level of 1.1. Nitroprusside stopped, hydroxocobalamin, nicardipine, then orals with amlodipine 5 added. Creatinine 2.8 at worst, 1.6 at discharge.

Today: feels himself again, wife agrees he's back to his usual. No headache. Taking all meds including the amlodipine. No dizziness or fainting.
Home BP 130s/80s.

Exam: BP 138/84. Alert, conversational, oriented, at his baseline. Heart regular. Lungs baseline. No edema.
Lab today: creatinine 1.4, potassium normal.

A/P
1. Hypertensive emergency, resolved. Now on amlodipine 5 + lisinopril 10 + HCTZ 25. Watch for light-headedness given carotid sinus hypersensitivity; so far fine.
2. Cyanide toxicity from nitroprusside, resolved without lasting deficit. Documented in the problem list so any future admission sees it.
3. CKD 2 with the creatinine still coming down from the admission. Repeat at June visit.
4. PMF, heme in May.
Med reconciliation done. RTC 6-7 weeks.

Continue ruxolitinib 5 mg twice daily. Return August.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after April admission.
Doing well. No headaches, no dizziness, no fainting. No blood in urine. Walking daily. Memory unchanged per wife. Taking amlodipine, lisinopril, HCTZ, tamsulosin, ruxolitinib, vitamin D.
Home BP log (finally written down): 124-136 / 74-84.

Exam: BP 132/80, at goal for the first time in two years. Heart regular. Lungs scattered wheezes, baseline. Spleen tip palpable, unchanged. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. HTN at goal on three agents. Continue amlodipine 5.
2. CKD 2: creatinine back to 1.2 today. UACR sent.
3. Carotid sinus hypersensitivity: no recurrence, precautions continue.
4. PMF: heme following, August visit.
5. HM: AWV in September, flu and COVID then, FIT due, CT in November.
RTC September.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Bernard, kidney function is back to where it was before the hospital (creatinine 1.2), potassium normal, and the urine protein is in your usual range. Keep doing exactly what you're doing. See you in September.
